text:
alex: Quick sketch — proposal for a "gradual diversion" rollout model -> a lightweight alternative to our existing canary+fallback pipeline. Idea: divert a small percentage of traffic to new variant, keep primary path live, and run an automated recovery path that can re-merge or eject without an immediate full fallback.

sam: hmm, how is this different from our staged canaries?

alex: Two main diffs: 1) diversion keeps requests routed through primary runtime for full observations (latency/cost) while mirroring + letting variant run in parallel on a subset, 2) recovery is policy-driven and can do split-adjust + soft eject rather than instant cutover. goal is less blast radius on perf regressions.

jordan: sounds useful for perf-sensitive endpoints. what about cold-starts / kv cache heat? if variant is cold we might see false negatives.

maria: good call. we should add a warmup phase where the variant receives a small steady-state stream for N minutes to populate caches, then start diversion.

kevin: operationally we need clear interfaces between router, observer, and evictor. right now those are pretty coupled in runtime. Alex — do you have an interface sketch?

alex: yeah — rough public API:

```
diversion.create({
  variant_id,
  percent,
  warmup_seconds,
  signals: ["latency_p95","error_rate","cost_delta"],
  recovery_policy: { type: "soft-eject", threshold: {error_rate: 0.01}, adjust_step: 0.1 }
})

diversion.status(variant_id) -> {diverted_percent, health, last_probe}
```

alex: Router implements divert-by-cookie/header for sticky sessions. Observer consumes telemetry and emits a compact signal stream (per-variant). Evictor adjusts percentages or nukes variant based on recovery_policy.

sam: want to point out signal fidelity concerns — telemetry backend adds 10s scrape lag. we need probe-level counters closer to runtime for SLO-bound decisions.

maria: agree. propose a small runtime probe shim that exports immediate counters and a control endpoint `/probe/variant/<id>` that returns health summary in <500ms. Observer can fall back to aggregated metrics if shim unavailable.

jordan: and what about A/B experiments with user-scoped buckets? can diversion coexist with experiments?

alex: yes — diversion should be orthogonal. Router applies experiment bucketing first, then diversion overlay for rollout percentages. if the variant is part of an experiment cohort, we honor experiment allocation and decrement diversion percent proportionally.

kevin: rollback automation risk: if we soft-eject in small steps, a regression could linger and slowly ramp down but still impact users. need a fast-stop circuit.

alex: include a "hard-stop" rule: if any critical signal crosses an absolute threshold (e.g., 5xx spike > 0.05), evictor triggers immediate removal and optionally triggers a canary-alert to oncall.

sam: how will this play with Dedicated/Private deployments where routing is region/tenant pinned?

maria: runtime config should allow scope: {global, region, tenant}. Default global, but customers (or deploys for Private) can lock to region/tenant semantics. Diversion controller must respect tenant isolation — no cross-tenant mirroring.

jordan: telemetry/observability: we need per-variant traces + tokenized cost breakdown to compare token-cost deltas. Recommend we include a lightweight sample of full traces (1 in 1000) for variants.

alex: agreed. Also include cost_delta signal from router that estimates token diff and flags quantization/precision regressions.

kevin: followups: 1) define the runtime probe API contract, 2) implement observer shim prototype that reads probe + metrics, 3) add control plane DSL for recovery_policy. I'll open tickets.

alex: thanks. I'll draft a short RFC with sequence diagrams and sample DSL (will include warmup semantics, sticky routing, and hard-stop triggers).

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: @alex/rfc-gradual-diversion v0.1 -> drafts (link: https://redwood-internal/rfc/3467890123) :rocket:

maria: one more ops note — add a cross-check to ensure the variant's model artifact is compatible with routing (kv-format, max-seq). incompatible variants should be rejected at create-time with clear error codes.

sam: nice. also add a telemetry TTL config so we don't keep high-cardinality variant metrics forever.

alex: cool — I'll incorporate. if nobody objects, I'll post the RFC later today for review. :thumbsup:
